lines: A synthesised bass drum: one oscillator whose frequency is bent on each hit, a square sub-oscillator under it, and a burst of pink noise for the beater click.
Sets the oscillator frequency, 60Hz at the centre of the knob and 5Hz for each step either side, so 35Hz at one end and 85Hz at the other.
Adds to the PITCH knob at 5Hz per volt, with no clamp on the result.
Sets the decay time of the envelope that bends the oscillator frequency; the knob runs from -0.2 to 1.2 seconds and the value used is held between 0 and 2.2 seconds.
Adds to the PITCH DECAY knob at 1 second per volt, with the total held between 0 and 2.2 seconds.
Sets the decay time of the envelope on the drum's level; the knob runs from -5 to 5 seconds and the value used is held between 0 and 2.2 seconds, so much of its travel does nothing.
Adds to the AMP DECAY knob at 1 second per volt, with the total held between 0 and 2.2 seconds.
Crossfades between the main oscillator at one end and the square sub-oscillator at the other.
Multiplies the whole voice by 0 to 10 before the output clips at ±5V, so the upper part of its travel drives the drum into distortion.
Sets the level of the pink noise burst that opens each hit, 0 to 2.5V before the drive is applied.
Chooses how far below the main oscillator the sub-oscillator runs: the same frequency, an octave down, or two octaves down.
Chooses a sine or a square wave for the main oscillator; the sub-oscillator is a square either way.
Starts a hit each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
The drum's audio, clipped to ±5V.
Note — the length of the gate changes nothing: each hit releases its two envelopes a fixed fraction of a second after the trigger, and the noise click is shorter again.
Note — the pitch envelope is subtracted from the oscillator frequency rather than added, so the frequency dips at the start of a hit and climbs back to what PITCH sets.
SyntheticBassDrum.notes: The maker names no port. PITCH CV is scaled 5Hz per volt rather than one volt per octave (src/controller/SBD.cpp:41), so it is a plain CV input and not a pitch input. The envelope release and the noise burst are fixed divisions of the sample rate at src/controller/SBD.cpp:61 and :67, not controls. The SUB OCT and WAVE switches are three-way and two-way slide switches; their panel markings are -2/-1/-0 and SIN/SQR.

lines: A clock generator running from 30 to 200 beats per minute, with whole, half, quarter, eighth and sixteenth outputs and six more carrying the Linn Drum swing timings.
Sets the tempo, from 30 to 200 beats per minute; the value is cut to a whole number before the clock uses it.
Adds to the BPM knob at 17 beats per minute per volt, with the total clamped between 30 and 200.
Sets how long each output stays at 5V, from 10 to 60 per cent of a sixteenth note.
Adds to the WIDTH knob at 5 per cent of a sixteenth note per volt, with the total clamped between 10 and 60 per cent.
Starts and stops the clock; each press flips it, and the lamp is lit while it runs.
Flips the clock between running and stopped each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
Chooses whether the six swing outputs pulse on eighth notes or on sixteenth notes.
Returns the count to the first sixteenth of the bar each time the voltage rises through 0.5V, and starts the clock running whether or not it was stopped.
5V for the set width on the first sixteenth of each bar, once every four beats.
5V for the set width on the first and the ninth sixteenth of each bar, twice every four beats.
5V for the set width on every fourth sixteenth, once per beat.
5V for the set width on every second sixteenth, twice per beat.
5V for the set width on every sixteenth of the bar.
A pulse train at the rate the SWING switch sets, evenly spaced, which is the 50 per cent entry of the Linn Drum swing table.
A pulse train at the rate the SWING switch sets, with every second pulse pushed late by 8 per cent of a sixteenth note, the 54 per cent Linn Drum swing timing.
A pulse train at the rate the SWING switch sets, with every second pulse pushed late by 16 per cent of a sixteenth note, the 58 per cent Linn Drum swing timing.
A pulse train at the rate the SWING switch sets, with every second pulse pushed late by 24 per cent of a sixteenth note, the 62 per cent Linn Drum swing timing.
A pulse train at the rate the SWING switch sets, with every second pulse pushed late by 32 per cent of a sixteenth note, the 66 per cent Linn Drum swing timing.
A pulse train at the rate the SWING switch sets, with every second pulse pushed late by 42 per cent of a sixteenth note, the 71 per cent Linn Drum swing timing.
Note — the clock comes up running and needs nothing patched into it; the green panel shows the tempo and the pulse width as numbers.
Note — every output here is either 0V or 5V, and all eleven are driven from one 16-step count of a four-beat bar.
Gnome.notes: The maker names no port. Panel names come from the rendered panel; the /1 to /16 and /A to /F labels sit below their jacks. src/controller/Gnome.cpp:58-59 comments that the tempo is rounded to a tenth, but the cast to uint16_t cuts it to a whole number. The two numeric displays are plain widgets with no parameter, so they cannot be clicked. The BPM and WIDTH jacks share their panel label with the knob beside them.

lines: A sixteen-step drum sequencer with eight gate tracks, sixteen storable patterns and an eight-slot chain that plays those patterns in order.
Switches that step of that track on or off; a step that is on sends a gate from its track's jack when the sequence reaches it.
Starts and stops the sequencer; each press flips it, and the lamp is lit while it runs.
Raises the number of the pattern loaded on the pads by one, to a maximum of 16.
Lowers the number of the pattern loaded on the pads by one, to a minimum of 1.
Raises the pattern number in that slot of the chain by one, to a maximum of 16.
Lowers the pattern number in that slot of the chain by one; at 0 the slot is skipped, and the first slot never goes below 1.
Chooses whether the sequencer moves on to the next chain slot at the end of the sixteen steps or keeps repeating the pattern now loaded.
Copies the sixteen by eight grid now on the pads into a holding buffer.
Writes the grid held by COPY onto the pads, replacing the pattern now loaded.
Advances the sequence by one step each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.

Sequencer.notes: The maker names no port. A pulse width knob and its CV input are declared but commented out of the panel at src/view/Sequencer.cpp:62-68, so the gate length is stuck at the parameter's default of 5.05, which src/controller/Sequencer.cpp:155-159 turns into 505 samples. Input index 4 is that CV jack and has no census position, so it gets no line. The 128 pads are separate parameters with their own positions, so each one can be clicked; they are numbered by track times sixteen plus step, which the maker's own tooltip names confirm. Pattern selection by voltage is 10V divided by 17 (src/controller/Sequencer.cpp:4-14), about 0.588V per pattern.

lines: An envelope generator for drums that runs a whole attack, decay, sustain and release cycle from one trigger, with every stage given its own length in seconds.
Sets how long the envelope takes to climb from 0V to its peak, from 0.001 to 4.999 seconds.
Adds to the attack time, 10V covering the whole 0.001 to 4.999 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall from its peak to the sustain level, from 0.001 to 4.999 seconds.
Adds to the decay time, 10V covering the whole 0.001 to 4.999 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets how long the envelope holds at the sustain level before it releases, from 0.001 to 4.999 seconds.
Adds to the sustain time, 10V covering the whole 0.001 to 4.999 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets the level the envelope holds at, as a fraction of the 5V peak; the value is clamped to 0.99, so the upper part of the knob gives one level and the panel's 0 to 5 marking is wrong.
Adds to the sustain level, 10V covering the 0.01 to 0.99 span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall from the sustain level to 0V, from 0.001 to 4.999 seconds.
Adds to the release time, 10V covering the whole 0.001 to 4.999 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Chooses a straight line or a quarter-sine curve for that stage; the panel prints EXP for the curve, which is a sine rather than an exponential.
Starts the envelope from 0V each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
The envelope, 0V to 5V.
Note — the envelope runs its whole shape from a trigger rather than from the length of a gate: the sustain stage has a time of its own, and the release follows it however long the gate stays high.
Baronial.notes: The maker names no port. A ninth parameter, DIRECTION, is declared at src/controller/Baronial.hpp:10 but is given no widget and is never read, so it has no census position and gets no line. The SUSTAIN LEVEL knob is configured 0.001 to 4.999 with a unit of Volts (src/controller/Baronial.cpp:24) but is used as a 0.01 to 0.99 fraction of the peak (src/controller/Baronial.cpp:42), so both the tooltip unit and the panel's 0 to 5 marking are wrong. The three curve switches choose between a straight line and sinf(x*pi/2) (src/model/Envelope.hpp:141, :171, :212); the panel prints LIN and EXP.

lines: A hybrid bass drum: a recorded kick blended with a sine oscillator, a square-to-sine sub-oscillator under them, and two envelopes shaping pitch and level.
Sets the decay time of the pitch envelope, from 0.1 to 2.2 seconds; at exactly 1 second the whole pitch envelope is turned upside down.
Adds to the pitch envelope's decay time, 10V covering a 0 to 2.2 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets the level the pitch envelope holds at, from 0.1 to 0.9 of its peak.
Adds to the pitch envelope's sustain level, 10V covering the 0.1 to 0.9 span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets the release time of the pitch envelope, from 0.1 to 2.9 seconds.
Adds to the pitch envelope's release time, 10V covering the 0.1 to 2.9 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Nothing in the module reads this switch; the pitch envelope is turned upside down by the pitch DECAY knob reaching exactly 1 second instead.
Replaces the pitch envelope with the voltage here divided by 5 for as long as a cable is patched, and the pitch DECAY, SUSTAIN and RELEASE knobs then do nothing.
Sets the decay time of the amplitude envelope, from 0.1 to 2.2 seconds; at exactly 1 second the whole amplitude envelope is turned upside down.
Adds to the amplitude envelope's decay time, 10V covering a 0 to 2.2 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets the level the amplitude envelope holds at, from 0.1 to 0.9 of its peak.
Adds to the amplitude envelope's sustain level, 10V covering the 0.1 to 0.9 span, with the total clamped to it.
Sets the release time of the amplitude envelope, from 0.1 to 2.9 seconds.
Adds to the amplitude envelope's release time, 10V covering the 0.1 to 2.9 second span, with the total clamped to it.
Nothing in the module reads this switch; the amplitude envelope is turned upside down by the amplitude DECAY knob reaching exactly 1 second instead.
Replaces the amplitude envelope with the voltage here divided by 5 for as long as a cable is patched, and the amplitude DECAY, SUSTAIN and RELEASE knobs then do nothing.
Restarts the sample from its first frame and retriggers both envelopes each time the voltage rises through 0.5V.
Multiplies the sample playback rate and both oscillator frequencies together, from 0.2x to 1.8x.
Adds to TUNE, 10V covering the 0.2 to 1.8 span, with the total clamped to it.
Crossfades between the sine oscillator and the recorded kick, 0 for all oscillator and 10 for all sample, despite the panel marking the knob 0 to 5.
Adds to BLEND, 10V covering its 0 to 10 span, with the total clamped to it.
Chooses which of the two recorded kicks plays; the choice also sets the oscillator frequency, which is twice the chosen sample's nominal 55Hz or 60Hz.
The drum's audio: the blended sample and oscillator with the sub-oscillator mixed in and the amplitude envelope applied, at 5V for a full-scale sample.
Sets how much of the sub-oscillator is in the output; the knob reaches half of the full mix and the CV input is needed for more.
Adds to the sub-oscillator mix, 10V covering the full 0 to 10 span, with the total clamped to it.
Chooses how far below the oscillator the sub-oscillator runs: the same frequency, an octave down, or two octaves down.
Crossfades the sub-oscillator between a square wave at one end and a sine at the other.
Adds to the sub-oscillator wave blend, 10V covering the full square to sine span, with the total clamped to it.
Note — both envelopes hold their sustain for a fixed 4400 samples before releasing, so the length of the gate changes nothing.
Note — the panel and the manual each give the two envelopes a DIRECTION switch, and neither switch is read by the module.
MarionetteBass.notes: The maker names no port. Both DIRECTION switches are dead: src/controller/Marionette.cpp:63 and :91 test PITCH_DECAY_PARAM and AMP_DECAY_PARAM against 1.0 rather than the switch parameters, which was confirmed in the shipped binary — pitchEnvelope loads params[0] and ampEnvelope params[4], never params[3] or params[7]. An input at index 6 (AMP_ATTACK_CV_IN) and an output at index 1 (ENVELOPE_OUT) are declared but given no widget and never read or written, so they get no line. BLEND is configured 0 to 10 (src/controller/Marionette.cpp:15) while the panel marks the knob 0 to 5. SUB MIX is configured 0 to 5 but read over a 0 to 10 span (src/controller/Marionette.cpp:140), so the knob alone cannot reach a full sub mix.
